get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of leave applications for the account. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

Results can be scoped to an approval tab with the `status` query parameter; when it is omitted the request is redirected so that `status=all` is applied by default.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `status` | Approval tab to list. One of `all`, `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `pending_on_me`. Defaults to `all`. |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter by a field, e.g. `filter[staff_id][equal]=1`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`. |
| `fields[]` | Restrict the returned columns. |
| `search` | Free-text search. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | `filter[id][equal]=5` |
| `staff_id` | integer (staff) | `filter[staff_id][equal]=1` |
| `type` | enum (`leave`, `half_leave`, `delay`, `early`) | `filter[type][equal]=leave` |
| `date_from` | date | `filter[date_from][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `date_to` | date | `filter[date_to][less_than_equal]=2026-12-31` |
| `created` | datetime | `filter[created][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `approved_by` | integer (staff) | `filter[approved_by][equal]=3` |
| `shift_type` | enum (`primary`, `secondary`) | `filter[shift_type][equal]=primary` |

Filter by approval state with the `status` tab parameter (above), not `filter[status]`. In practice the endpoint accepts a filter on any existing column.

**Sortable fields.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc`. The field intended for sorting:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `created` | datetime | `sort[created]=desc` |

When no `sort` is given, results are returned newest-first (by `id`, descending). In practice the endpoint accepts a sort on any existing field.

The response is a standard paginated envelope; each item in `data` is a leave-application record. Which staff members' applications are returned depends on the caller's leave permissions (own applications, or those they may view/approve for others).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Approval tab to list: `all`, `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `pending_on_me`. Defaults to `all`.

200.description: A paginated list of leave applications.

data.description: The leave applications on this page. Each item is a leave-application record.

staff_id.description: Id of the staff member the leave is for.

created_by.description: Id of the staff member who created the application.

400.description: The list could not be produced — for example the leave-application entity is unavailable for this account or the required plugin is inactive.

error.description: Reason the request failed (e.g. the leave-application entity is unavailable for the account, or the required plugin is not active).

401.description: The Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a single leave application by id. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page or format flag.

The successful response is a **flat object** of the leave application's fields (it is not wrapped in a `data` envelope). It also embeds the `attachments` array and related records: the applicant staff (`staff_leave_application`), the leave type (`leave_application_type`), the creator staff (`leave_application_creator`), the approver staff (`leave_application_approver`), the linked attendance permission (`leave_application_attendance_permission`), and the approval-cycle configuration (`approval_cycle_configuration`). Related records are `null` when not applicable.

Note: requesting an id that does not exist currently returns HTTP 500 with the plain-text body `error happened` rather than a 404.

parameters.name: ID
parameters.description: The id of the leave application to fetch.

200.description: The leave application, returned as a flat object with embedded relations.

schema.description: A single leave-application record, returned flat (not wrapped).

staff_id.description: Id of the staff member the leave is for.

type.description:
Leave type.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| leave | Leave |
| half_leave | Half (½) Leave |
| delay | Late Arrival |
| early | Early Leave |

leave_type_id.description: The configured leave type id (set for `leave` / `half_leave`).

status.description:
Approval status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| pending | Pending |
| approved | Approved |
| rejected | Rejected |

approved_by.description: Id of the staff member who approved/rejected the application.

created_by.description: Id of the staff member who created the application.

attendance_permission_id.description: Id of the attendance permission created when the leave is approved.

shift_type.description: Shift the leave applies to, when applicable.

approval_data.description: Multi-cycle approval state, when an approval cycle applies.

approval_cycle_configuration_id.description: Id of the matched approval-cycle configuration, when applicable.

attachments.description: Files attached to the leave application.

leave_application_creator.description: The staff record that created the application.

leave_application_approver.description: The staff record that approved/rejected the application, or null.

leave_application_attendance_permission.description: The linked attendance permission, or null.

approval_cycle_configuration.description: The matched approval-cycle configuration, or null.

401.description: The Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired.

schema.description: Plain-text body `error happened`. Currently returned when the requested id does not exist (rather than a 404).

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a leave application for a staff member. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. The request body is a **flat JSON object** whose keys are the leave-application fields.

Always provide `staff_id`, `date_from`, `date_to` and `days`. The date range and day count must be consistent: `date_to` must equal `date_from + (days − 1)` (and be on or after `date_from`).

Which other fields are required depends on `type`:

| `type` | Meaning | Additionally required |
|---|---|---|
| `leave` (default) | Leave | `leave_type_id` |
| `half_leave` | Half (½) Leave | `leave_type_id` |
| `delay` | Late Arrival | `late_time` (minutes) |
| `early` | Early Leave | `early_time` (minutes) |

Do **not** send `id` (assigned automatically), `status` (always starts as `pending`), `approved_by`, `created_by` (taken from the authenticated user) or the approval-cycle fields (resolved automatically). On success the endpoint returns the standard native-entity `{ message, id }` envelope with the new leave-application id.

> Known issue (dev): the create pipeline currently faults and returns HTTP 500 `{"message":"Server Error"}` for this entity — see the audit report. The request contract below is the intended one.

staff_id.description: Required. Id of the staff member the leave is for. The caller must be allowed to apply leave for that staff member.

date_to.description: Required. Last day of leave, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Must be on or after `date_from` and equal to `date_from + (days − 1)`.

days.description: Required. Number of leave days requested.

type.description:
Optional. Kind of application. Defaults to `leave`.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| leave | Leave |
| half_leave | Half (½) Leave |
| delay | Late Arrival |
| early | Early Leave |

leave_type_id.description: Required when `type` is `leave` or `half_leave`. The configured leave type to use.

description.description: Optional. Free-text note stored on the application.

attachments.description: Optional. Uploaded files attached to the application (max 5 MB each).

200.description: The leave application was created; the standard native-entity `{ message, id }` envelope is returned with the new id.

id.description: Id of the created leave application.

400.description: The leave application could not be saved. On a validation failure the body is `{ "message": "Entity not saved", "errors": { … } }` with per-field messages in `errors` (a required field missing, or a field invalid for the chosen `type`); on a database save failure it is the `{ e, message, error }` envelope.

message.description: Failure summary — `Entity not saved` on a validation or save failure.

errors.description: Present on a validation failure: per-field messages keyed by field name (e.g. a missing `staff_id`/`date_from`/`date_to`/`days`, or a `leave_type_id` omitted for a `leave`/`half_leave` application).

e.description: Present on a database save failure: error detail object (or empty array).

error.description: Present on a database save failure: failure detail.

401.description: The Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired.

500.description: Currently returned by the create pipeline for this entity on dev (`{"message":"Server Error"}`); no record is inserted. Recorded as a known issue in the audit report.

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing leave application, identified by the `{ID}` path segment. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. The request body is a **flat JSON object** of leave-application fields.

Provide the fields to change. The record is re-validated, so keep the date range and day count consistent: `date_to` must equal `date_from + (days − 1)` and be on or after `date_from`. Conditional requirements follow `type` exactly as on create:

| `type` | Meaning | Additionally required |
|---|---|---|
| `leave` | Leave | `leave_type_id` |
| `half_leave` | Half (½) Leave | `leave_type_id` |
| `delay` | Late Arrival | `late_time` |
| `early` | Early Leave | `early_time` |

Server-managed fields cannot be changed here: `status` (moved by the approval workflow, not this endpoint), `approved_by`, `created_by` and the approval-cycle fields. The `comment` field can only be set when the application is created — it is not editable here (send it on create instead). On success the standard native-entity `{ message, id }` envelope is returned.

> Known issue (dev): the update pipeline currently faults and returns HTTP 500 `{"message":"Server Error"}` for this entity (the target row is left unchanged) — see the audit report. The contract below is the intended one.

parameters.name: ID
parameters.description: The id of the leave application to update.

staff_id.description: Id of the staff member the leave is for.

date_to.description: Last day of leave, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Must be on or after `date_from` and equal to `date_from + (days − 1)`.

type.description:
Kind of application.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| leave | Leave |
| half_leave | Half (½) Leave |
| delay | Late Arrival |
| early | Early Leave |

attachments.description: Optional. Files attached to the application (max 5 MB each). Editable on update.

200.description: The leave application was updated; the standard native-entity `{ message, id }` envelope is returned.

id.description: Id of the updated leave application.

400.description: The update failed. Three shapes: `{ "message": "Record not found" }` when the `{ID}` does not exist; `{ "message": "Entity not saved", "errors": { … } }` when required fields are missing or invalid for the chosen `type` (per-field messages in `errors`); or the `{ e, message, error }` envelope on a database save failure.

message.description: Failure summary. `Record not found` when the `{ID}` does not exist; `Entity not saved` on a validation or save failure.

errors.description: Present on a validation failure: per-field messages keyed by field name (e.g. a missing `staff_id`/`date_from`/`date_to`/`days`).

e.description: Present on a database save failure: error detail object (or empty array).

error.description: Present on a database save failure: failure detail.

401.description: The Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired.

500.description: Currently returned by the update pipeline for this entity on dev (`{"message":"Server Error"}`); the target row is left unchanged. Recorded as a known issue in the audit report.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of attendance logs for the account. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. On this endpoint the data level has no visible effect, so `/attendance_log/list` and `/attendance_log/list/1` return the same result. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter by a field (see the Filterable fields table below). |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`. |
| `fields[]` | Restrict the returned columns. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `staff_id` | integer (staff) | `filter[staff_id][equal]=1` |
| `status` | enum | `filter[status][equal]=draft` |
| `source_type` | enum (`machine`, `supervisor`, `file`, `self`) | `filter[source_type][equal]=self` |

In practice the endpoint accepts a filter on any existing column.

**Sorting.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc` (e.g. `sort[time]=desc`). No field is specifically flagged as sortable in the metadata, but the endpoint accepts a sort on any existing column; with no `sort`, results are returned newest-first.

The response is a standard paginated envelope; each item in `data` is a flat attendance-log record.

Each record's `status` is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Draft |
| sign_in | Sign In |
| sign_out | Sign Out |
| repeated_sign_in | Repeated Sign In |
| repeated_sign_out | Repeated Sign Out |
| invalid | Invalid |
| unknown_employee | Unknown Employee |

and `source_type`, when present, is one of `machine`, `supervisor`, `file`, `self`.

200.description: A paginated list of attendance logs.

data.description: The attendance logs on this page. Each item is an attendance-log record.

staff_id.description: Id of the employee the log belongs to.

session_id.description: Id of the attendance session, when applicable.

status.description:
Log status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Draft |
| sign_in | Sign In |
| sign_out | Sign Out |
| repeated_sign_in | Repeated Sign In |
| repeated_sign_out | Repeated Sign Out |
| invalid | Invalid |
| unknown_employee | Unknown Employee |

source_id.description: Id of the source that produced the log, when applicable.

source_name.description: Name of the source, when applicable.

source_type.description:
Source of the log.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| machine | Machine |
| supervisor | Supervisor |
| file | File |
| self | Self |

source_method.description: How the source recorded the log, when applicable.

invalidity_reason.description:
Why the log is invalid, when applicable.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| weekend | Weekend |
| on_leave | On Leave |
| no_shift | No Shift Assigned |
| out_of_shift_boundaries | Out of Shift Boundaries |

400.description: The list could not be produced — for example the attendance-log entity is unavailable for this account or the required plugin is inactive.

error.description: Reason the request failed (e.g. the attendance-log entity is unavailable for the account, or the required plugin is not active).

401.description: Authentication or authorization failed. A missing, invalid, or expired Bearer token returns a plain `401` (no JSON body). An authenticated caller who lacks permission to view attendance logs receives `{ "error": "You are not allowed to view this page" }`.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Adds an attendance log. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The request body is a flat JSON object. Only `staff_id` and `time` are required; every other field is optional. The combination of `time` + `staff_id` must be unique — posting the same pair twice fails.

The `status` and `source_type` value tables below are the recognized sets; note the API does not currently validate them on input — an unrecognized value is accepted (stored coerced), not rejected.

`status` defaults to `draft` when omitted:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Draft |
| sign_in | Sign In |
| sign_out | Sign Out |
| repeated_sign_in | Repeated Sign In |
| repeated_sign_out | Repeated Sign Out |
| invalid | Invalid |
| unknown_employee | Unknown Employee |

`source_type`, when supplied, is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| machine | Machine |
| supervisor | Supervisor |
| file | File |
| self | Self |

staff_id.description: Required. Id of the employee the log belongs to.

time.description: Required. Log timestamp, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. Must be unique per employee (`time` + `staff_id`).

status.description:
Optional. Defaults to `draft` when omitted. Recognized values are below, but note this field is **not validated on input** — an unrecognized value is accepted and stored coerced (empty), not rejected.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Draft |
| sign_in | Sign In |
| sign_out | Sign Out |
| repeated_sign_in | Repeated Sign In |
| repeated_sign_out | Repeated Sign Out |
| invalid | Invalid |
| unknown_employee | Unknown Employee |

session_id.description: Optional. Id of the attendance session the log belongs to.

source_type.description:
Optional. Recognized source values below (not validated on input):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| machine | Machine |
| supervisor | Supervisor |
| file | File |
| self | Self |

source_id.description: Optional. Id of the source that produced the log.

source_method.description: Optional. How the source recorded the log.

id.description: Id of the newly created attendance log.

400.description: The attendance log could not be saved — for example the `time` + `staff_id` combination already exists.

error.description: Reason the record could not be saved — for example a duplicate `time` + `staff_id` combination.

401.description: The Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired.

422.description: A required field is missing or invalid. `errors` maps each failing field to its messages (e.g. `staff_id` or `time` omitted).

errors.description: Per-field validation messages, keyed by field name.
